summary: My project was created using Pygame Zero and Mu. It is designed for children who dream of traveling to the Moon and exploring life in space. Players can manage a lunar base by planting, growing, and harvesting crops, as well as receiving real-time communications. The project aims to reach children nationally and internationally through an educational and entertaining experience. It includes two minigames: one about planting and harvesting crops, and another about unscrambling words. Its main purpose is to encourage creativity, curiosity, and learning about space exploration while allowing children to have fun and imagine life on the Moon.
details: Hi! I’m Sarah Diez, from Medellín, and I’d like to introduce my project, "EarthSignal." My inspiration came from lunar craters—I was really intrigued by how they might have formed and what the Moon would be like without them. For my research, I looked into studies on lunar agriculture—specifically, the "Veggie" mission. My game is based on space missions on the Moon, such as planting crops and receiving messages. Right now, it only has two stations, but I plan to add more soon.I designed my project using Pygame Zero and wrote the code in Mu. I want my project to reach children with imaginations as vast as my own—kids who dream of traveling to the moon or experiencing what it would be like to manage tasks there, such as planting and harvesting crops or receiving real-time communications. I want this project to reach children both nationally and internationally—kids all over the world. It includes two minigames: one focused on planting, and another that involves unscrambling words.
